source.title: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
source.authors: Zhi-Li Feng; Yixuan Even Xu; A. Robey; Robert Kirk; Xander Davies; Yarin Gal; Avi Schwarzschild; J. Kolter

page_placements.theme: Recovery baselines: never-trained or retrained references also 'recover', and relearning speed reflects more than retained information
Measurement artifacts in MCQ and attack-based evaluation (both forgetting and recovery)

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether finetuning and input-space attacks reveal targeted information, and whether the result depends on evaluation format, using its own experiments rather than reproducing one original method and measure.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports cited results from other work, including Łucki et al.'s five-sample RMU result; these are not recorded as this study's results. Figure 2 tests generalization on a base Phi-1.5 that had not seen the forget set, not recovery from an unlearned model, so it is described under fits_no_version. Figure 3 is illustrative rather than an experimental result. Some graph values are not legible in the supplied text; those are marked figure only.
record.test_reason: The paper runs its own finetuning attacks (Fig 4, 6) and Enhanced GCG attacks (Fig 5) on RMU and NPO unlearned models, plus ACR extraction tests (Fig 7, Table 1). It uses these results to argue that the evidence for recovery (B, E) depends on answer format, data format and information injection, and so may overstate shallowness. These are results plus a specific argument that versions need restating, which is T5 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue existing adversarial unlearning evaluations (finetuning, Enhanced GCG, ACR) are inconclusive. Attacks can inject information (spurious retain-forget generalization, high-capacity prefixes), and outcomes vary with task and answer format. Evaluations may therefore both overstate and understate unlearning success. They propose minimal information injection and downstream task awareness, with an injection budget and cross-format leakage matrices.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates existing RMU/NPO checkpoints with finetuning, Enhanced GCG and ACR; it does not reproduce any of the three named original studies' full recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Finetuning effectiveness changes with whether relearning and unlearning data formats match. Apparent recovery changes between maximum letter probability, maximum text probability and open-ended generation. ACR conclusions also differ across CHOOSE, OPTION and GENERATE tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Finetuning base Phi-1.5 (which never saw TOFU) on 100/200/500 TOFU-MCQ items raises held-out TOFU-MCQ accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benchmark retain and forget splits share spurious structure, so retain-set relearning can raise forget accuracy without any hidden knowledge.

fits_no_version.finding: A GCG prefix optimized on a test-overfit Llama-3.2-1B using 7 samples raises the base model's WMDP-Bio accuracy from 39.9% to 53.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimized adversarial prefixes can inject answer information, so prompt-based recovery need not show retained knowledge.

record.problems: Experiments use a small number of unlearning methods and academic benchmark datasets, as the authors acknowledge. Several results are available only in figures in the supplied text. The evaluation results depend on task and answer format, and the authors note that their information-injection measures are heuristic.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 7 results for WMDP-Chem and WMDP-Cyber across all model/task combinations are not separately extracted; the text gives only qualitative summaries and the plotted values are not reliably assignable from the supplied flattened figure text. Table 1's remaining ACR model-by-dataset cells (including NPO-Cyber) are omitted to prioritize the RMU/NPO-Bio comparisons and the task-dependent results. Figures 4 and 6 curves are represented by their tested model/format conditions rather than separate rows for every plotted finetuning sample count.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy on standard MCQ before attacks and general-capability benchmarks (e.g. MMLU) are not measured; general ability is inferred only from WMDP-Chem ACR/success rates.
Relearning on a subset of forgotten facts and on unrelated data; only WMDP-Bio retain-set samples are used.
Entire version: no activation-direction ablation or internal analysis.
Rephrasing, other languages, multi-turn jailbreaks and in-context information; only the Enhanced GCG optimized prefix is tested.
Entire version: no robust counter-method proposed or tested.

missing.what: Fig 5 full values: MCQ panel Base 0.644 / RMU 0.299 / RMU+GCG 0.539; generation panel Base 0.597 / RMU 0.106 / RMU+GCG 0.263. Needed to correct the r13/r14 baselines.
Fig 7 RMU forget-set results on WMDP-Cyber (RMU was unlearned on Cyber) and NPO-Cyber on Cyber, across the three tasks; only the Bio rows are extracted.
Non-target WMDP-Chem success rates: RMU similar to Base, NPO lower, for CHOOSE and OPTION (general-ability evidence).

record.verdict_notes: Changed tranche from T2 to T5: the paper's purpose is to argue the shallow-unlearning evidence is confounded. The information-capacity argument (about 1430 bits of answers versus about 1500 bits in a 100-token prefix) concerns Łucki et al.'s cited result and is an argument, not a new row. The 29.9%/62.4%/64.4% figures in §3.1 are cited from Łucki et al. and correctly excluded. Fig 6's checkpoint identities (MCQ- or corpora-unlearned) are not stated. Most finetuning results are figure-only, so the B states rest on the authors' prose.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish that targeted accuracy was near chance before each attack or systematically assess preservation of general ability.
Tests relearning with specified WMDP/TOFU data and formats; does not test recovery from a subset of forgotten facts or all kinds of unrelated/loosely related examples.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit experiment; evaluation concerns do not demonstrate that a particular unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests Enhanced GCG optimized prefixes, not ordinary rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information.
No new counter-method is tested for resistance to these attacks.

tranche.reason: The paper argues that finetuning, Enhanced GCG and ACR evaluations are inconclusive and that recovery results depend on format and information injection. That fits T5, not the reader's T2.

The Fig 6 data format isn't stated, and 'MCQ data' for RMU (r9, r11) conflicts with §4.1. r15's 53.8% is on the non-finetuned Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. l3 should cover RMU only.
